title: Cerebral Palsy and the GMFCS: Levels I to V, Hips and Goals

hook.en: Two children have the same diagnosis but live completely different movement lives. The GMFCS explains why, and it tells you what to aim for and what to watch, especially the hips.
hook.ur: Do bachon ki tashkhees ek hai magar un ki harkat ki zindagi bilkul mukhtalif hai. GMFCS batata hai kyun, aur yeh bhi ke kis cheez ka hadaf rakhein aur kis par nazar, khaas kar hips par.

goal.en: By the end, you'll define cerebral palsy, classify a child's gross motor function on the GMFCS (I to V) by age band, link the level to hip risk and goals, and know the other classification systems and red flags.
goal.ur: End tak aap cerebral palsy ki tareef karenge, bachay ke gross motor function ko GMFCS (I se V) par umar ke band ke hisab se classify karenge, level ko hip risk aur goals se jorenge, aur doosre classification systems aur red flags jaanenge.

text.en: **Cerebral palsy (CP)** is a group of **permanent disorders of movement and posture** caused by a **non-progressive** disturbance in the developing fetal or infant brain. It is the commonest cause of physical disability in childhood, roughly 2 per 1,000 live births. The motor problem is often joined by problems of sensation, perception, thinking, communication, behaviour, epilepsy and, over time, **secondary musculoskeletal problems** such as contracture, hip displacement and scoliosis. The brain injury does not progress, but the body's response to it does, which is why growth is the physiotherapist's moving target.
text.ur: **Cerebral palsy (CP)** **harkat aur posture ke mustaqil masail** ka group hai jo barhte hue janeen ya shireer dimagh mein **ghair-progressive** nuqsan se hota hai. Yeh bachpan ki jismani maazoori ki sab se aam wajah hai, taqreeban 1,000 zindah paidaishon mein 2. Motor masle ke saath aksar sensation, idrak, sochne, communication, rawaiye ke masail, epilepsy aur waqt ke saath **secondary musculoskeletal masail** (contracture, hip displacement, scoliosis) jurte hain. Dimagh ki chot aage nahi barhti magar jism ka us par rad-e-amal barhta hai, isi liye barhta hua jism physiotherapist ka harakat karta hadaf hai.

text.en: Picture **two children in the same school but at different gates**. The label "cerebral palsy" is the school's name; the **GMFCS level** is which gate the child uses. A child at Level I walks through the main entrance (he walks anywhere, but his speed and balance are limited). A child at Level III uses the side gate with a handrail (a walker indoors, a wheelchair for distance). A child at Level V is carried through the lift (full support and transport). Same school, different routes, so the plans for each gate are different too.
text.ur: **Ek hi school ke do bachay magar mukhtalif darwazon par** tasawwur karein. "Cerebral palsy" ka label school ka naam hai; **GMFCS level** yeh hai ke bachcha kaunsa darwaza istemal karta hai. Level I wala bachcha mukhya darwazay se guzarta hai (har jagah chalta hai, magar raftaar aur balance mehdood). Level III wala bachcha railing wale side gate se (ghar mein walker, faaslay ke liye wheelchair). Level V wala bachcha lift mein utha kar le jaya jata hai (mukammal sahara aur transport). Ek hi school, mukhtalif raaste, is liye har darwazay ka plan bhi alag hai.

intro.en: Pick a level, then an age band: the descriptor changes because the same level looks different at 18 months and at 14 years. The bar shows the approximate risk of hip displacement for that level, and below it is the usual physiotherapy focus. Compare Level II and Level III at 6 to 12 years: the key difference is the handheld device.
intro.ur: Level chunein, phir umar ka band: descriptor badalta hai kyunke ek hi level 18 mahine aur 14 saal par mukhtalif dikhta hai. Bar us level mein hip displacement ke taqreeban risk ko dikhata hai, aur uske neeche aam physiotherapy focus hai. 6 se 12 saal par Level II aur Level III ka muqabla karein: aham farq haath mein pakra hua device hai.

question.en: A 9-year-old walks at school with a walker, climbs stairs holding a rail with help, and uses a manual wheelchair for outings. Which GMFCS level?
question.ur: 9 saal ka bachcha school mein walker se chalta hai, madad se rail pakar seerhi chadhta hai aur bahar jane ke liye manual wheelchair istemal karta hai. Kaunsa GMFCS level?

text.en: Level V: transported in a wheelchair in all settings
text.ur: Level V: har jagah wheelchair mein le jaya jata hai

feedback.en: Level V children cannot walk and have very limited head and trunk control. This child walks with a walker.
feedback.ur: Level V bachay chal nahi sakte aur sar aur dhar ka control bohat mehdood hota hai. Yeh bachcha walker se chalta hai.

text.en: Level III: walks using a handheld mobility device, wheeled mobility for distance
text.ur: Level III: haath mein pakre device se chalta hai, faaslay ke liye wheeled mobility

feedback.en: Yes — Level III children walk with a handheld device indoors and use wheeled mobility for longer distances or outdoors.
feedback.ur: Haan — Level III ke bachay ghar mein haath ke device se chalte hain aur lambay faaslay ya bahar ke liye wheeled mobility istemal karte hain.

text.en: Level I: walks without limitations
text.ur: Level I: bina rukawat chalta hai

feedback.en: Level I children walk anywhere without a device; speed and balance are mildly limited.
feedback.ur: Level I bachay baghair device har jagah chalte hain; raftaar aur balance halke mehdood.

hint.en: The deciding feature is what he uses to walk at school: a handheld device.
hint.ur: Faisla kun cheez yeh hai ke school mein chalne ke liye woh kya istemal karta hai: haath ka device.

text.en: The **GMFCS (Expanded and Revised)** classifies a child's **usual, self-initiated gross motor performance** in everyday settings, with emphasis on sitting, transfers and mobility, in five levels and five age bands (under 2, 2 to 4, 4 to 6, 6 to 12, 12 to 18 years). It asks "what does the child usually do?", not "what can he do on his best day?" and not how good the movement looks. The **distinctions that matter**: between I and II (limits in running, jumping, balance and long distances), between II and III (does the child need a handheld mobility device to walk?), between III and IV (does he walk or mainly use powered mobility?) and between IV and V (head and trunk control).
text.ur: **GMFCS (Expanded and Revised)** bachay ki **aam, khud shuru ki hui gross motor performance** ko rozmarrah mahol mein, baithne, transfers aur harkat par zor ke saath, paanch levels aur paanch umar ke bandon (2 se kam, 2 se 4, 4 se 6, 6 se 12, 12 se 18 saal) mein classify karta hai. Yeh poochta hai "bachcha aam taur par kya karta hai?", "achhe din mein kya kar sakta hai?" nahi, aur harkat kitni achhi lagti hai woh bhi nahi. **Aham farq**: I aur II ke beech (bhagne, kudne, balance aur lambay faaslay mein hadood), II aur III ke beech (kya bachay ko chalne ke liye haath ka mobility device chahiye?), III aur IV ke beech (kya woh chalta hai ya zyada tar powered mobility?) aur IV aur V ke beech (sar aur dhar ka control).

question.en: A 5-year-old walks well indoors and outdoors, climbs stairs without help, and is just starting to run and jump, though more slowly and clumsily than other children. Which level?
question.ur: 5 saal ka bachcha ghar ke andar aur bahar achi tarah chalta hai, baghair madad seerhi chadhta hai, aur bhagna kudna shuru kar raha hai, magar doosray bachon se aahista aur anari tarah. Kaunsa level?

text.en: Level III
text.ur: Level III

feedback.en: Level III children need a handheld device to walk. This one does not.
feedback.ur: Level III bachon ko chalne ke liye haath ka device chahiye. Isse nahi.

text.en: Level I
text.ur: Level I

feedback.en: Yes — he walks without a device and without limits; reduced speed, balance and coordination are the Level I limitation.
feedback.ur: Haan — woh baghair device aur rukawat chalta hai; kam raftaar, balance aur coordination Level I ki hadd hai.

text.en: Level II
text.ur: Level II

feedback.en: Level II children walk but may need a rail on stairs and cannot run or jump much. This child climbs stairs freely.
feedback.ur: Level II bachay chalte hain magar seerhi par rail chahiye aur bhag kood zyada nahi kar sakte. Yeh bachcha azadi se seerhi chadhta hai.

title.en: The other classification systems that go with the GMFCS
title.ur: GMFCS ke saath doosray classification systems

rows.en: Gross motor function: sitting, transfers, walking (Levels I to V)
rows.ur: Gross motor function: baithna, transfers, chalna (Levels I se V)

rows.en: Sets goals, equipment and hip surveillance level
rows.ur: Goals, equipment aur hip surveillance ka level tay karta hai

rows.en: Manual ability: how the child handles objects in daily life (Levels I to V)
rows.ur: Manual ability: bachcha rozmarrah mein cheezein kaise sambhalta hai (Levels I se V)

rows.en: Plans hand therapy, adaptations and school tasks
rows.ur: Haath ki therapy, adaptations aur school ke kaam plan karta hai

rows.en: Communication function, and eating and drinking ability
rows.ur: Communication function, aur khane peene ki salahiyat

rows.en: Spots communication and swallowing risk, which strongly shape quality of life and safety
rows.ur: Communication aur nigalne ka khatra pehchanta hai, jo zindagi ki quality aur hifazat par bohat asar rakhte hain

text.en: **Confusing the GMFCS with a measure of progress or ability.** The GMFCS level describes a stable pattern; it is **not** a score that should "improve" with therapy, and a child's best performance in the clinic does not change the level. Treating a child at Level III as if he were "almost Level II" sets families up for disappointment. Another error is classifying by the **diagnosis label** (spastic diplegia means "walks") instead of the actual function. And the most dangerous one: attributing every new loss of skill to "CP getting worse". CP does not progress, so new regression needs a new explanation.
text.ur: **GMFCS ko progress ya salahiyat ka paimana samajhna.** GMFCS level ek mustaqil pattern bayan karta hai; yeh aisa score **nahi** jo therapy se "behtar" ho, aur clinic mein bachay ki behtareen performance level nahi badalti. Level III wale bachay ko "taqreeban Level II" samajhna families ko mayoosi ke liye tayyar karta hai. Ek aur ghalti: asal function ke bajaye **tashkhees ke label** (spastic diplegia ka matlab "chalta hai") se classify karna. Aur sab se khatarnaak: har naye hunar ke kho jane ko "CP ka bigarna" kehna. CP aage nahi barhti, is liye nayi regression ki nayi wajah dhoondni chahiye.

title.en: Hip surveillance in cerebral palsy: the plan that prevents dislocation
title.ur: Cerebral palsy mein hip surveillance: woh plan jo dislocation se bachata hai

steps.title: Classify the child by GMFCS
steps.detail: The level sets how often the hips need a check. || Bachay ko GMFCS se classify karein

steps.title: Take a baseline pelvis X-ray
steps.detail: An AP pelvis view, typically by about 2 years, then repeated at the interval your local protocol sets for the GMFCS level. || Baseline pelvis X-ray lein

steps.title: Measure the migration percentage
steps.detail: Reimers MP is the part of the femoral head that lies outside the acetabulum, as a percentage of the head's width. About 30% or more is the usual "at risk" threshold. || Migration percentage naapein

steps.title: Add the clinical exam
steps.detail: Hip abduction range, pain, asymmetry, leg length and Thomas test; a loss of abduction is an early clue. || Clinical exam shamil karein

steps.title: Act early and teach positioning
steps.detail: Rising MP means an urgent orthopaedic referral; day-to-day, support symmetrical positioning, supported standing and sleeping postures that keep the hips in abduction. || Jaldi amal karein aur positioning sikhayein

text.en: **Goals from the level.** For a Level I child: running, hopping, balance, sport and fitness. For Level II: stairs, uneven ground, endurance, and the choice of a wheelchair for long distances without guilt. For Level III: efficient walker use, orthoses, transfers, and a wheelchair for community distances. For Level IV and V: seating, powered mobility, supported standing, comfort and safe handling. For everyone: set **child- and family-chosen goals** (for example "go to the shop with my cousins"), use **goal-directed, task-specific practice** with repetition at the right dose, and write the GMFCS level in every report.
text.ur: **Level se goals.** Level I bachay ke liye: bhagna, hop, balance, khel aur fitness. Level II: seerhiyan, na-hamwar zameen, endurance, aur lambay faaslay ke liye wheelchair ka intekhab bina sharminda hue. Level III: walker ka behtar istemal, orthoses, transfers, aur community faaslay ke liye wheelchair. Level IV aur V: seating, powered mobility, supported standing, aaram aur mehfooz handling. Sab ke liye: **bachay aur family ke chune hue goals** (maslan "cousins ke saath dukan jana") tay karein, **goal-directed, task-specific mashq** sahi dose ki repetition ke saath karein, aur har report mein GMFCS level likhein.

text.en: Hip displacement rises steeply with the GMFCS level: in a population-based study from Australia, the rate of hip displacement (migration percentage over 30%) was about **0% at Level I, 15% at II, 41% at III, 69% at IV and 90% at V**. Regular surveillance programmes that detect displacement early have sharply cut the number of dislocated hips and salvage operations where they have been used. For early detection, the **General Movements Assessment** and the Hammersmith examination can identify a high risk of CP before 6 months, which opens the door to early, goal-directed intervention. Gross motor function tends to plateau in early childhood, earlier at the more severe levels, and may decline in adolescence at Levels III to V without maintenance.
text.ur: Hip displacement GMFCS level ke saath tezi se barhta hai: Australia ki population-based study mein hip displacement (migration percentage 30% se zyada) ki sharah taqreeban **Level I par 0%, II par 15%, III par 41%, IV par 69% aur V par 90%** thi. Jahan regular surveillance programmes istemal hue wahan unhon ne displacement jaldi pakar kar dislocated hips aur salvage operations ki tadad bohat kam ki. Shuruati pehchan ke liye **General Movements Assessment** aur Hammersmith examination 6 mahine se pehle CP ke zyada khatre ki nishandahi kar sakte hain, jo jaldi, goal-directed mudakhilat ka darwaza kholta hai. Gross motor function shuruati bachpan mein plateau par aati hai, shadeed levels par jaldi, aur Levels III se V mein adolescence mein maintenance ke baghair ghat sakti hai.

text.en: **Treat these as red flags in a child with CP:** new or worsening hip, back or limb pain (hip displacement, fracture, a pain source the child cannot report), new loss of skills or new limb weakness (consider a tethered cord, a shunt problem, an infection or a different diagnosis), increased seizures, drooling with chest infections (aspiration), a sudden rise in tone (look for a noxious trigger such as a urinary infection, constipation, a pressure sore or an ingrown toenail), and fragile bones in non-walking children (osteopenia: handle limbs gently, and support the joints during transfers and stretching). Never force a stretch through pain.
text.ur: **CP wale bachay mein yeh red flags samjhein:** naya ya barhta hip, kamar ya limb ka dard (hip displacement, fracture, aisa dard jo bachcha bata nahi sakta), naya hunar kho dena ya limb ki nayi kamzori (tethered cord, shunt ka masla, infection ya mukhtalif tashkhees par ghaur karein), barhte daure, seene ke infections ke saath laar tapakna (aspiration), tone ka achanak barhna (peshab ka infection, qabz, pressure sore ya andar ki taraf barhta nakhun jaise trigger dhoondein), aur na chalne wale bachon mein nazuk haddiyan (osteopenia: limbs ko narmi se handle karein, transfers aur stretching mein joints ko sahara dein). Dard ke bawajood stretch zabardasti na karein.

prompt.ur: Kaunsa classification system is sawal ka jawab deta hai?

text.en: Does the child need a walker to walk at school?
text.ur: Kya bachay ko school mein chalne ke liye walker chahiye?

why.en: Gross motor mobility belongs to the GMFCS.
why.ur: Gross motor mobility GMFCS ka hissa hai.

text.en: How does the child pick up, hold and release objects in daily tasks?
text.ur: Bachcha rozmarrah ke kamon mein cheezein kaise uthata, pakarta aur chhorta hai?

why.en: That is manual ability: the MACS.

text.en: Can the child chew and swallow safely?
text.ur: Kya bachcha mehfooz tareeqe se chabata aur nigalta hai?

why.en: Eating and drinking ability: the EDACS.

text.en: Can the child make their needs understood to familiar people?
text.ur: Kya bachcha jaanay pehchanay logon ko apni zaroorat samjha sakta hai?

text.en: Can he get from the floor to standing without help at age 7?
text.ur: Kya woh 7 saal ki umar mein farsh se baghair madad khara ho sakta hai?

why.en: Floor-to-stand transfers are a GMFCS distinction between levels.
why.ur: Farsh se khara hona levels ke darmiyan GMFCS ka farq hai.

question.en: Why does a child at GMFCS Level V have a much higher risk of hip displacement than one at Level I?
question.ur: GMFCS Level V wale bachay mein Level I ke muqable mein hip displacement ka khatra kahin zyada kyun hai?

answer.en: The hip socket and femoral head are shaped by **load and movement** in growth. A child who never stands or walks has little weight-bearing to deepen the socket, plus strong adductor and flexor tone and weak abductors pulling the head up and out. Over years the head slides out of the socket (the migration percentage rises). The risk grows with the level because standing and walking, which protect the hip, are less available. This is why **supported standing, abduction positioning and early surveillance** are not optional extras.
answer.ur: Hip socket aur femoral head ki shakal barhne ke dauran **bojh aur harkat** se banti hai. Jo bachcha kabhi khara nahi hota ya chalta nahi uske socket ko gehra karne ke liye weight-bearing kam hoti hai, saath mazboot adductor aur flexor tone aur kamzor abductors head ko upar aur bahar kheenchte hain. Saalon mein head socket se bahar phisalta hai (migration percentage barhta hai). Khatra level ke saath barhta hai kyunke khara hona aur chalna, jo hip ki hifazat karte hain, kam mumkin hotay hain. Isi liye **supported standing, abduction positioning aur jaldi surveillance** laazmi hain, optional nahi.

question.en: A 6-year-old child with CP at GMFCS Level IV, who uses a power chair, has two weeks of new pain on the left side of the groin that hurts when his hips are moved, and he has lost his ability to stand in his stander. What should you do?
question.ur: 6 saal ka bachcha jis ko CP hai, GMFCS Level IV, power chair istemal karta hai, left groin mein do hafte se naya dard hai jo hips hilne par barhta hai, aur woh stander mein khara hone ki salahiyat kho chuka hai. Aap kya karenge?

text.en: Stop the stretching and standing, treat it as a possible hip displacement or fracture and arrange an urgent medical and X-ray review
text.ur: Stretching aur standing rok dein, ise mumkin hip displacement ya fracture samjhein aur foran medical aur X-ray review karwayein

feedback.en: Yes — new pain with loss of function in a high-risk child (and fragile bones) needs imaging before any further loading.
feedback.ur: Haan — zyada khatre wale bachay (aur nazuk haddiyon) mein naya dard aur function ki kami ke saath koi mazeed load dalne se pehle imaging chahiye.

text.en: Increase the stretching to restore the range
text.ur: Range behal karne ke liye stretching barha dein

feedback.en: Forcing a stretch on a possibly displaced or fragile hip can cause a fracture.
feedback.ur: Mumkin tor par displaced ya nazuk hip ko zabardasti stretch karne se fracture ho sakta hai.

text.en: Continue as planned; pain is part of cerebral palsy
text.ur: Plan ke mutabiq jaari rakhein; dard CP ka hissa hai

feedback.en: Pain is common but never "normal": it needs a cause, especially a hip.
feedback.ur: Dard aam hai magar kabhi "normal" nahi: iski wajah dhoondni chahiye, khaas kar hip.

summary.en: CP is a group of permanent, non-progressive disorders of movement and posture from an early brain injury; the secondary musculoskeletal problems grow over time.
summary.ur: CP shuruati dimagh ki chot se harkat aur posture ke mustaqil, ghair-progressive masail ka group hai; secondary musculoskeletal masail waqt ke saath barhte hain.

summary.en: The GMFCS (I to V, by age band) describes what a child usually does: Level I walks anywhere, II with limits, III with a handheld device, IV mainly powered mobility, V transported.
summary.ur: GMFCS (I se V, umar ke band ke hisab se) batata hai ke bachcha aam taur par kya karta hai: Level I har jagah chalta hai, II hadood ke saath, III haath ke device ke saath, IV zyada tar powered mobility, V le jaya jata hai.

summary.en: The level predicts hip risk (about 0% at Level I to about 90% at Level V), so surveillance, supported standing and abduction positioning are part of the plan, and new pain or lost skills are red flags.
summary.ur: Level hip risk ka andaza deta hai (Level I par taqreeban 0% se Level V par taqreeban 90%), is liye surveillance, supported standing aur abduction positioning plan ka hissa hain, aur naya dard ya hunar kho dena red flags hain.

back.en: Permanent disorders of movement and posture from a non-progressive disturbance in the developing fetal or infant brain, often with other problems (sensation, cognition, epilepsy).
back.ur: Barhte hue janeen ya shireer dimagh mein ghair-progressive nuqsan se harkat aur posture ke mustaqil masail, aksar doosray masail (sensation, idrak, epilepsy) ke saath.

back.en: The child's usual gross motor function (sitting, transfers, mobility) in five levels and five age bands.
back.ur: Bachay ka aam gross motor function (baithna, transfers, harkat) paanch levels aur paanch umar ke bandon mein.

front.en: What separates Level II from Level III?
front.ur: Level II aur Level III mein kya farq hai?

back.en: Level III children need a handheld mobility device to walk and use wheeled mobility for distance; Level II walk without a device in most places.
back.ur: Level III bachon ko chalne ke liye haath ka mobility device chahiye aur faaslay ke liye wheeled mobility; Level II aksar jagah baghair device chalte hain.

front.en: How does hip risk change with GMFCS level?
front.ur: GMFCS level ke saath hip risk kaise badalta hai?

back.en: About 0% at Level I, 15% at II, 41% at III, 69% at IV and 90% at V for migration over 30%.
back.ur: Migration 30% se zyada ke liye Level I par taqreeban 0%, II par 15%, III par 41%, IV par 69% aur V par 90%.

front.en: What is the Reimers migration percentage?

back.en: The share of the femoral head lying outside the acetabulum on an AP pelvis X-ray; about 30% or more is considered at risk.
back.ur: AP pelvis X-ray par femoral head ka woh hissa jo acetabulum se bahar hai; taqreeban 30% ya zyada khatre mein samjha jata hai.
